A layer that expands the spatial dimensions $x$ and $y$ of an input volume $U$ of size $x \times y \times p$ by factors $s_x$ and $s_y$ respectively to generate a volume $V$ of size $(s_x x) \times (s_y y) \times p$ [S2, unofficial].

The claim states that a layer expands spatial dimensions x and y of an input volume U (size x × y × p) by factors sx and sy to generate volume V (size (sx x) × (sy y) × p). Section 3.2.4 of Source [S2] explicitly states: 'Upsampling layers simply expands the spatial dimensions x and y of the input volume U of size x × y × p by sx and sy respectively to generate a volume V of size (sx x) × (syy) × p.' The claim matches this description exactly (noting that 'syy' in the source is a typo for 'sy y'). Additionally, the claim mentions the input/output dimensions and expansion factors, which are fully supported by the text.

It explains that this method maps full-resolution voxels to a double-resolution volume and states that 'the double-resolution volume allows the existing voxel to be located at the middle point between two voxels of the full-resolution volume leading to precise shape and contour of the object,' thereby addressing issues where 'non-corresponding pixels... are possibly mapped to the same voxel' due to the discrete domain. This directly supports the claim that the technique corrects discrete positioning errors.
